question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay that wins over mutable config and blocks weakening writes, or keep immutable baseline handling in Policy/Nix-style conformance surfaces?
rationale: The request changes security boundaries, config precedence, write rejection behavior, diagnostics, and upgrade expectations; current main only has adjacent conformance checks and scoped write guards.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, conflict checks for config writes, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only policy
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for audits while runtime config stays the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer until hook design settles
options.body: Leave this issue open while related policy-hook proposals clarify whether enforcement belongs in plugin hooks, core config/write paths, or both.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, conflict checks for config writes, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns this issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest security-boundary decision owner.
